text: A plan covers Hartwell's policy decisions: scope, severity scale, communication chain. A runbook is narrower and tactical -- the specific steps a responder actually follows, in the moment, for the incidents Hartwell is realistically going to see.
Mara structures the runbook around six phases: Triage, Scope, Contain, Eradicate, Recover, and After-action. Each one has concrete, Hartwell-specific actions, not generic advice.

Triage asks whether an alert is real or noise. Scope asks what else it touches. Contain stops it from getting worse without destroying evidence -- the specific account, the specific address, not the whole system.
The runbook defines severity tiers, SEV1 through SEV4, with concrete criteria, decided now, calmly, instead of improvised during a real alert at 3 a.m.

Writing this runbook before any real incident has happened is deliberate -- so the next alert this project's new correlation rule produces has somewhere concrete to go. Next lesson, that rule fires for real.
